Ministry Of Skill Development And Entrepreneurship. Implemented between FY 2022-2026 under the \"Skill India Programme\", the scheme component \"Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 - Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)\" by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India aims to certify candidates who already possess prior-learning experience or skills, with emphasis on upskilling and horizontal skilling within the same NSQF level, so that they obtain industry-relevant skill certification. Through this scheme component, pre-screening, mandatory orientation/training, assessment, and a graded skill certificate, along with one-year accidental insurance and a T-shirt, are provided to candidates with prior learning experience or skills who are willing to get assessed and certified. The scheme is implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), the implementing arm of MSDE, through Recognition of Prior Learning Project Implementing Agencies (RPL-PIAs) responsible for overall execution, with assessment and certification by NCVET-approved Awarding Bodies (ABs) and Assessment Agencies (AAs).. The scheme aims to certify the existing skills of experienced candidates. Through this scheme, free assessment, upskilling, certification, and insurance are provided to Indian candidates.. Industry-relevant skill certification for candidates with prior learning experience or skills, through due assessment. Mandatory training/orientation of a minimum of 30 hours in a classroom setting, with the maximum duration of RPL being 132 hours. Pre-screening of candidates by certified trainers to assess their existing level of learning; no payment is charged to the candidate for pre-screening. Assessment and Certification, with a payout of ₹600 per candidate per assessment provided to the Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) / Awarding Bodies for overseeing and facilitating final assessments. Accidental Insurance with one year of coverage, paid from the scheme (as per prevailing rates, ₹14.16). Launched in 2015, with its 4.0 phase being implemented between Financial Year 2022 and Financial Year 2026, the scheme \"Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 – Special Projects\" by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India, aims to meet the skilling needs of marginalized and vulnerable groups, difficult geographies, and specialized training courses that are likely to be offered outside of regular short-term skilling programmes, and can also focus on new-age job roles with future skills. Through this scheme, project-based short-term skilling initiatives — which can be residential or non-residential and may avail certain exemptions granted with the approval of the Executive Committee are provided to marginalised and vulnerable groups and candidates in difficult geographies that require special attention. The scheme is implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), which supports the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), and is delivered on the ground through Special Projects Implementing Agencies (SPIAs). Objectives of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 The scheme promotes an enabling ecosystem for the youth to get skilled and choose a career path aligned with their abilities and aspirations. The scheme enables delivery of skill training in a market-oriented and demand-driven manner, with emphasis on improving the employability of candidates. The scheme simplifies processes of the skill ecosystem by leveraging technology and digitalisation. The scheme enhances access to skilling by setting up skill development infrastructure in remote and difficult geographies such as hilly terrain, Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areas, and border areas, by designing special projects. The scheme improves inclusivity by ensuring that Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), women, and other marginalised communities can undertake skill training and access gainful wages and self-employment.
